blocks.content: 1.1 Ancient Tamil History – Sangam Age

The Sangam Age refers to the period roughly between 300 BCE and 300 CE. It is named after the Sangam assemblies of Tamil poets held in Madurai under the patronage of the Pandya kings. The Sangam literature comprises over 2,300 poems by more than 470 poets, providing invaluable insights into the social, economic, and political life of ancient Tamils.

The Three Crowned Kings (Moovendar) were the Chera, Chola, and Pandya dynasties. They frequently fought each other and with minor chieftains (Velir). The port of Puhar (Kaveripoompattinam) was a major centre of Indo-Roman trade.
Key Sangam Works

cells: Oldest extant Tamil literary work; grammar and poetics
400 poems on war, death, and heroism
Story of Kovalan and Kannagi; written by Ilanko Adigal

blocks.content: 1.2 Early Medieval Dynasties
The Pallavas (275 CE – 897 CE)

The Pallavas ruled from Kanchipuram and were great patrons of art and architecture. Their rock-cut temples and structural temples at Mahabalipuram (Mamallapuram) are UNESCO World Heritage Sites. The Pallava script is the ancestor of many South and Southeast Asian scripts.

items: Notable rulers: Simhavishnu, Mahendravarman I, Narasimhavarman I (Mamalla), Narasimhavarman II (Rajasimha), Aparajitavarman
Architectural style: Dravidian architecture – Rathas (monolithic) and Shore Temple
Defeated by the Chalukyas and later by the Cholas

blocks.content: The Early Cholas

The Cholas had their capital at Uraiyur and later at Kaveripoompattinam. Karikala Chola is the most celebrated early Chola king. He built the Grand Anicut (Kallanai) across the Kaveri River, one of the oldest water regulation structures in the world still in use.
1.3 Medieval Tamil Nadu – The Imperial Cholas (850 CE – 1279 CE)

The Imperial Chola dynasty is one of the longest-ruling dynasties in the world's history. Founded by Vijayalaya Chola who captured Thanjavur from the Mutharaiyars in 848 CE, the dynasty reached its zenith under Rajaraja Chola I and Rajendra Chola I.

cells: Conquered Madurai; defeated Kerala and Sri Lanka
Built Brihadeeswarar Temple; conquered Sri Lanka and Maldives
Gangaikonda Cholapuram; naval expedition to Southeast Asia
United Chola and Chalukya kingdoms; abolished tolls

blocks.content: Brihadeeswarar Temple – Key Facts

items: Built by Rajaraja Chola I in 1010 CE
Vimana (tower) is 66 metres high – tallest in India at the time
The Nandi (bull) statue is carved from a single rock
UNESCO World Heritage Site (Great Living Chola Temples)

blocks.content: 1.4 The Pandyas

The Pandya dynasty ruled from Madurai. They were great patrons of Tamil literature and the legendary sponsors of the Tamil Sangams. The Later Pandyas (1190–1345 CE) saw the dynasty reach its peak under Maravarman Sundara Pandya and Jatavarman Sundara Pandya I, who defeated the Hoysalas and expanded into Andhra and Sri Lanka.
The Pandya kingdom was devastated by the invasion of Malik Kafur (general of Alauddin Khilji) in 1310 CE and later subjugated by the Vijayanagara Empire.
1.5 The Vijayanagara Empire (1336–1646 CE)

Founded by Harihara I and Bukka Raya I, the Vijayanagara Empire played a crucial role in protecting South India from Delhi Sultanate invasions. The empire's capital was at Hampi (Karnataka). Tamil Nadu formed the eastern part of the empire, governed by Nayak governors.
The Nayaks of Madurai, Thanjavur, and Gingee became independent after the fall of Vijayanagara following the Battle of Talikota (1565 CE).
The Nayak Period

items: Madurai Nayaks (1529–1736): Tirumala Nayak built the Thirumalai Nayakkar Mahal; constructed the Meenakshi Amman Temple complex
Thanjavur Nayaks (1532–1673): Patronized Telugu literature; fortified Thanjavur
Gingee Nayaks: Built the impregnable Gingee Fort

blocks.content: 1.6 Maratha Rule in Thanjavur (1674–1855 CE)

Venkoji (Ekoji), the half-brother of Shivaji, established Maratha rule in Thanjavur after defeating the last Thanjavur Nayak in 1674 CE. The Thanjavur Marathas were great patrons of art, music, and literature. The Saraswati Mahal Library in Thanjavur, with thousands of manuscripts in Tamil, Sanskrit, Telugu, and Marathi, was established during this period.
1.7 European Presence and British Rule
Portuguese, Dutch, Danish, French and British Presence
Fort St. George and Madras Presidency

The British East India Company established Fort St. George at Madras (Chennai) in 1639. Francis Day and Andrew Cogan obtained land from the Nayak of Chandragiri. The Madras Presidency was formally established and became one of the three major Presidencies of British India.
Polygar Wars (Palegars' War)

The Polygars (Palayakkarars) were local chieftains who controlled territories in southern Tamil Nadu. They resisted British control in the Polygar Wars (1799–1805). Veerapandiya Kattabomman of Panchalankurichi became a symbol of resistance against the British. He was captured and hanged at Kayathar in 1799 CE. Maruthu Pandiyar brothers continued the resistance and were executed in 1801 CE.

Key Personalities

blocks.content: The Non-Cooperation Movement (1920-22) and Civil Disobedience Movement (1930) had widespread participation in Tamil Nadu. The Salt Satyagraha saw Tamil activists make salt at Vedaranyam under T. Prakasam.
The Quit India Movement (1942) saw mass arrests across Tamil Nadu. Women like Ambujammal and Rukmini Lakshmipathi played crucial roles.
